_comment: Composable Survival English v4 scenario bank. The semantic composer preserves each frame's role/opener invariants, prefers frame-local user states, and applies at most one weighted persona/twist challenge axis. Public fields are user-visible; hidden_scene/ai_private and bank instructions are AI-only disclosure boundaries.

key_expressions.en: Honestly, I'm wiped. What about you?
key_expressions.function: Say you're tired, then hand the turn back

gloss.en: Say you're exhausted and pass the question back
gloss.ko: 피곤하다고 말한 뒤 상대에게 질문 넘기기

key_expressions.why: "Wiped" is how labmates actually talk at 7 pm. Handing the question straight back is what keeps small talk going.

key_expressions.en: I was thinking of grabbing something to eat — want to come?
key_expressions.why: "Do you want to have dinner with me" sounds like a date. "Grab something to eat" is the neutral colleague version.

key_expressions.en: I'd love to, but I've got an early start tomorrow.
key_expressions.function: Turn it down without sounding cold

gloss.en: Say no warmly, with a reason

key_expressions.why: A bare "no" ends the relationship as well as the plan. Warm opener plus a concrete reason is the standard shape.

key_expressions.en: Are you waiting for Professor Kim too?
key_expressions.function: Open with the thing you're both doing

gloss.en: Start a conversation from the shared situation
gloss.ko: 지금 둘 다 겪고 있는 상황으로 말 걸기

key_expressions.why: The easiest opener there is: you already have something in common, so no invention is required.

key_expressions.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
key_expressions.function: Ask for a name you missed

gloss.en: Ask for a name you didn't hear

key_expressions.why: Everyone misses names, including native speakers. Asking early is normal; asking twenty minutes later is the awkward version.

key_expressions.function: Close the chat when your turn comes
key_expressions.why: Short conversations need an ending too. "Anyway" is the signal English uses for "we're done here".
